title: refactor(plugin-auth): move the better-auth global after-hook into auth-manager-after-hook.ts (#25224 cut 12)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuMjbPDrsigsyqoKsV4WZQMz)_

Part of #25224
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none
Ruling-ref: 6348891160, 6364006498

The basis for the `Clause-②: no` line: this is a move. No accept set, route, refusal, code or answer changes, and the published surface is measured unchanged:
- `@objectstack/plugin-auth`'s `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.mts` are raw byte-identical to base (0 diff lines, so the union-order normalisation has nothing to do). The positive control is the one ruling `6348891160` asks for.
- Its ESM and CJS entries export the same 159 names at base and at head.

The `.d.ts` bar is ruling `6348891160` item 1 (on #25222, covering this card). Ruling `6364006498` is Sales's ruling A on this card. This is the fourth cut it applies to.

Cut 12 of the `auth-manager.ts` split: **the global after-hook of the better-auth instance**. It is the first of the three `createAuthInstance` slices the seat set (`hooks.after`, then `hooks.before`, then the rest of the method). #25224 stays open for the later cuts.

This follows the amended claim `6374301142`, which amends `6372234293` on the file cut 11 left (#25524, landed note `6373433471`). The shape is cuts 1 to 11's, which is #23050's, applied to a closure instead of a method. The seat ruled that in scope at 19:56Z, the same call as #25223's `start()` R3, with the bars listed below.

Branch: `claude/project-thread-lg3wrj`, the harness-pinned branch for this session, restarted from `origin/main` `1ff43b67ea` after #25524 merged. It names no issue, so the card relation is this body's first line.

`auth-manager.ts` goes from 8,536 to 8,362 lines. The cut is +274 / −193 over 2 files: 467 changed lines, under the 3,000-line line. It is not a governed surface (`check-governed-merges.mjs --branch HEAD`: NOT governed). One commit: `d79f55f402` `refactor(plugin-auth): move the better-auth global after-hook into auth-manager-after-hook.ts`.

## The move

| moved | base lines | proof lines | tokens | members it reads |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| the `hooks.after` arrow body in `createAuthInstance` | `:2834`–`:3016` | 185 | 610 | 8 methods |

The lines are base `1ff43b67ea`. The 185 proof lines are the body with its braces (`:2833`'s `{` to `:3017`'s `}`).

- **What it is:** `createAuthInstance` (`:1699`, private, annotated `Promise<Auth<any>>`) builds one config literal for better-auth. Its `hooks.after` is `createAuthMiddleware(async (ctx: any) => {BODY})`: the after-hook every better-auth endpoint's response passes through.
- **What BODY does, in order** (all of it moves, with its comments): the bearer rotation on impersonation, the echo of the installed session token, the session envelope completion, the two-factor re-enrolment reset, the sign-in outcome count with the refusal audit, the concurrent-session cap and the login stamp, the password-change stamp and history commit, the old-address notice on an e-mail change, the directory doors narrowed for an external caller, the invite-role refusal code, and the sign-up `disableSignUp` restore.
- **Where it goes:** a new module, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-after-hook.ts` (255 lines). BODY becomes the body of `export async function globalAfterHook(this: AfterHookHost, ctx: any)`, re-indented eight spaces (four levels) and otherwise unedited. The module header gives the reasoning, in the form the eleven earlier `auth-manager-*.ts` modules use.
- **What stays:** `createAuthInstance` keeps its place, docblock and signature, and `hooks.after` keeps its place in the literal. Its arrow is now:

  ```ts
  // [#25224 cut 12] The body moved to `auth-manager-after-hook.ts`; this
  // arrow hands it the members it reads (`AfterHookHost`).
  after: createAuthMiddleware((ctx: any) => {
    const host: AfterHookHost = {
      auditRefusedSignIn: (...a) => this.auditRefusedSignIn(...a),
      // … one closure per member, alphabetical, 8 in all
    };
    return globalAfterHook.call(host, ctx);
  }),
  ```

  Nothing else in `createAuthInstance` changes.

## The seat's bars

**Body.**
- BODY is the same TypeScript token sequence at base and in `globalAfterHook`: 185 lines, 610 tokens. Every line is the base line minus exactly eight spaces, and the parameter list (`ctx: any`) is the same text. Neither side has a return annotation.
- **`async` moves from the arrow to the function.** The head arrow is not `async`, and it returns `globalAfterHook.call(host, ctx)`, the function's own promise, unchanged. better-auth 1.7.12's `createAuthMiddleware` is better-call 1.4.4's `createMiddleware`, whose handler wrapper runs `const response = await _handler(internalContext);` inside its `try` (`dist/middleware.mjs:15`). So it awaits the same promise BODY settles, with the same value or rejection, and its `catch` sees the same error. The host literal and the `.call` cannot throw before that promise exists.
- **No captured locals.** None of the locals `createAuthInstance` declares before the literal (`betterAuth`, `createAuthMiddleware`, `setShouldSkipSessionRefresh`, `plugins`, `passwordHasher`) is read in BODY. The binding proof below finds no identifier in BODY bound anywhere else in the method either.
- **No `arguments`, `new.target` or `super`** (0 of each), where an arrow and a function differ. There is no bare `this`: BODY's only `this` uses are 9 member reads, `this.X`.

**Receiver.**
- BODY's `this` was the `AuthManager` instance, the arrow's lexical receiver. It is now the host.
- `AfterHookHost` names exactly the 8 members BODY reads, no more, each typed as the class member (`AuthManager['x']`): `auditRefusedSignIn`, `enforceConcurrentCap`, `externalDirectoryDoorDeps`, `recordPasswordHistory`, `recordSignInOutcome`, `sendChangeEmailNotice`, `stampLastLogin` and `stampPasswordChangedAt`.
- All 8 are methods, so each goes as a late-bound closure, `(...a) => this.x(...a)`. The method runs on the manager and is looked up when BODY calls it, so a spy or double set on the manager is still the one BODY reaches.
- BODY reads no field, so there is no getter. No member BODY reads is a function-valued field, so there is nothing to disclose the way #25516 disclosed `resolveKernelService`.

**Host lifetime.** The host is built inside the arrow, once per run of the hook: each time better-auth runs `hooks.after` on an endpoint's response. The seat allowed once per `createAuthInstance` call; this is more often, and it is what every method stub in this series does. Nothing BODY reads is captured early, because each closure looks its method up on the manager at call time.

**Readers.** The decision letters are read at both ends below: 4 drop, as expected. No anchor entry is owed. Tenant census and symbol-anchor output are byte-identical at both ends, and the full plugin-auth suite passes at both ends.

## Imports and evaluation order

Seven import lines leave `auth-manager.ts`, because BODY was their last reader there:
- `narrowDirectoryForExternalCaller` (the line stays as `import { type ExternalDirectoryDoorDeps } from './external-directory-door.js'`);
- `rotateCallerBearerOnImpersonation` (a three-line import block), `echoInstalledSessionToken`, `resetVerifiedOnTwoFactorReenrollment`, `codeInviteRoleNotFound`, `attachSessionToCredentialResponse` and `readRequestClientAddress`.

`SIGN_IN_EMAIL_PATH` has other readers in `auth-manager.ts`, so both files import it. One import line is added after cut 11's, with a comment in the same form: `import { globalAfterHook, type AfterHookHost } from './auth-manager-after-hook.js'`. The new module imports the `AuthManager` type only.

esbuild drops a type-only import, so a module whose last value import leaves `auth-manager.ts` is now first evaluated later, when the new module is reached. I read each top level:
- `two-factor-rotated-token-echo`, `two-factor-reenrollment-verified-reset`, `invite-role-not-found-code`, `session-envelope-completion` and `external-directory-door` are now reached only through the new module. None of the five imports anything. Their top levels are literals, interfaces and function declarations (plus two arrow consts in `external-directory-door`), so there is no side effect to reorder.
- `impersonation-bearer-rotation` is still reached earlier, through `admin-impersonate-endpoint.ts:137`.
- `request-client-address` is now first reached through `auth-manager-request-routing.ts`, before the new module. Its top level is one `defineRequestState(() => undefined)` from `@better-auth/core/context`, which creates a frozen ref object over the per-request store and registers nothing globally, so the order cannot be observed.
- The new module's own top level is imports, one interface and one function declaration. Its import of `auth-manager.ts` is type-only, so there is no runtime cycle.

## The decision-letter layer: −4, as expected

`check-adr-anchors`, measured at both ends. The gate exits 0 at both.

| point | anchored files | citations | files | decision letters |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| base `1ff43b67ea` | 83 | 52,270 | 6,675 | 1,971 |
| head `d79f55f402` | 83 | 52,270 | 6,676 | 1,967 |

- The four letters are in BODY's comments: ADR-0069 D2 (`:2882`, the account lockout counter), D7 (`:2904`, the login audit stamp) and D1 twice (`:2918` and `:2995`, the password-changed stamps). They leave `auth-manager.ts`, which is anchored, for a module that is not. Their citations still resolve, so the citation count does not move.
- **No entry is owed.** The `auth-manager.ts` entry has two paragraphs: ADR-0108 (better-auth's organization roles map) and ADR-0093 D2 (`settleMembership` and its two seams, `user.create.after` and `session.create.before`). Neither describes `hooks.after`, and no other entry names it. So, per the seat's bar, no entry is added for the new module.

## Path readers

No path reader needs migrating: none reads a moved line.
- **The tenant-audit census.** No census site moves: BODY has no engine write, no `this.X.delete()` and no elevation read. `check-tenant-audit-census` exits 0 at both with no `--write`, and its output is byte-identical. The `--json` document has 238 sites at both and 0 per-site differences with line numbers ignored. 2 sites are in `auth-manager.ts` at both (each 174 lines earlier at head, the cut's net), and 0 are in the new module. Only `scannedSources` (743 → 744) and `measuredAt` differ, so neither census document is edited.
- **`check-dispatcher-error-vocabulary.mjs`** and **`api-error-code.pin.test.ts`'s `authManagerFiles` floor**: BODY has no `new APIError(`. The gate reads 56 sites found and 56 classified at both; only its scanned-file count moves (3,420 → 3,421).
- **`check-auth-mount-ledger.mjs`**: no base-path literal or declaration is in BODY.
- **The plugin-factory scans** in `better-auth-schema-parity.test.ts` and `managed-extension-fields.test.ts` match `better-auth/plugins…` and `@better-auth/…` dynamic imports. BODY has no dynamic import, and both suites pass at head.
- **`rate-limit-storage-isolation.test.ts`** walks the import graph from `rate-limit-storage.ts`, which reaches neither file. It passes at head.
- **The system-context census** reads 149 elevation read sites at both, with byte-identical output.
- **Every symbol anchor into the file.** Before the cut, every `auth-manager.ts#symbol` anchor in the tracked tree outside changelogs was mapped with `symbolSegmentResolution` from `scripts/symbol-anchors.mjs`. There are 29, and all 29 are `declaration`-class at base, at base with BODY blanked, and at head. None of their symbols occurs as a token on a line of BODY.

## Proof

Builds and suites ran through `os-verify-lock`, and every exit code was captured before any pipe. Base `1ff43b67ea`. A full `turbo run build` ran first. Then `plugin-auth` was built and its suite run at base, and built and run again at head, on the same dependency dists.

**1. The moved text.**
- **Token identity:** the base arrow body and the module function body are the same TypeScript token sequence (scanner tokens, kind and text, trivia skipped, each template literal re-scanned at its substitutions as the parser does): 185 lines and 610 tokens, each line the base line minus eight spaces.
- **The head arrow's shape**, checked by the same run: not `async`, the same parameters, one host literal whose keys are exactly `AfterHookHost`'s and whose every value is `(...a) => this.<key>(...a)`, then `return globalAfterHook.call(host, ctx)`, and nothing else.
- **Binding identity:** a second proof walks all 181 identifiers of BODY at base and in the module, in order, and resolves each with the TypeScript checker. All 181 resolve the same way at both ends:
  - 38 to the `ctx` parameter;
  - 56 to a declaration inside BODY, the same declaring identifier by position;
  - 9 to the receiver's members (`AuthManager` at base, `AfterHookHost` at head);
  - 8 to imports with the same specifier and imported name;
  - 70 to no declaration: the globals `Error` and `undefined`, and property names on untyped values.

  None resolves to a `createAuthInstance` local or to a top-level declaration of either file.
- **Negative controls:** both proofs read the module text, and each control changes it in memory only; the file is untouched.
  - Token proof: `await rotateCallerBearerOnImpersonation(ctx);` changed to `void …` fails the token and line checks, and the run exits 1.
  - Binding proof: the module's `readRequestClientAddress` import pointed at another specifier gives 1 difference, and the run exits 1.
- **An independent reading:** `git diff --color-moved=plain --color-moved-ws=allow-indentation-change 1ff43b67ea d79f55f402` over the source files marks 188 of the 193 deleted lines and 194 of the 274 added lines as moved.
  - The 5 unmoved deletions are the `external-directory-door` import line (now type-only), the three-line `rotateCallerBearerOnImpersonation` import block (now one line in the module), and the `after: createAuthMiddleware(async (ctx: any) => {` line (now without `async`).
  - The other added lines are the module header, the host interface and its docblock, the function signature, the arrow's host literal and `return`, and the two new import comments and lines.

**2. `.d.ts` and exports (ruling `6348891160` items 1 and 2).**

| file | base and head | raw diff lines |
|---|---|---:|
| `dist/index.d.ts` raw | `1b3a48357d137155de33104277667a922aab62df73b418b03894c56faaacd0ba` | 0 |
| `dist/index.d.ts` normalised | `cee7303ccdfe72794efd588c85b628419d4253d730b5a0c5a3f1cdb8dddb4443` | |
| `dist/index.d.mts` raw | `b5e8dc982b634f0a5108b1b533626a68767f2da5a56f72dba801059b149e2872` | 0 |
| `dist/index.d.mts` normalised | `562d0a4ce656f97aeb937541482cdf531b61d7c75a005918784bf0a52d032dfc` | |

- The normaliser, verbatim (the ruling's one-liner): `node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1],"utf8");process.stdout.write(s.replace(/"[^"\n]*"(?:\s*\|\s*"[^"\n]*")+/g,r=>r.split(/\s*\|\s*/).sort().join(" | ")))' dist/index.d.ts | sha256sum`.
- The raw files are byte-identical, so no union-order swap occurs: items 1(b) and 1(d) hold with nothing to account for.
- **Positive control:** the head `dist/index.d.ts` with one private member made public (`private createAuthInstance;` → `createAuthInstance;`, line 1712, a one-line change) hashes raw `35b18682171cd394898c9e56bc8d5272ccf20aeff0d1966fc568cb5e566a08df` and normalised `e69c1b0157b45e48bbc16bd64eb939abf9be33ccb31553485df93ef05aac6fc3`. Both differ from the readings above.
- **Export lists:** ESM `dist/index.mjs` and CJS `dist/index.js` each have 159 names at base and at head, the same list (the sha256 of the sorted names is `3abb126f5babb701…` on all four). `globalAfterHook` and `AfterHookHost` are not among them, and `dist/index.d.ts` names neither.
- **The bundle:** 18 files in `dist/` at both, the same list. Only `index.js`, `index.mjs` and their two `.map` files differ, as a move of code inside the bundle must. `tsup` bundles the new module into the root entry (`splitting: false`).

**3. Tests and lint.**
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=3` in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth`: base `Test Files 191 passed (191)`, `Tests 3607 passed | 10 skipped (3617)`, exit 0. Head: the same counts, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck` (both `tsc` projects and `check:test-typecheck`): exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck`: exit 0.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` (the root `lint` script's binary and flags) over the 2 source files: exit 0.

**4. The censuses, the measurement and the anchors, at base and at head.**
- The tenant-audit census, as above: byte-identical gate output, 238 sites at both, 0 per-site differences line-blind, 0 unresolved and 0 unledgered at both.
- `scripts/measure-durability-swallow-family.mjs` (a measurement, not a gate): 77 members and 84 quiet rows at both. The members are the same with line numbers ignored, and the quiet rows are identical. Only the scanned file count moves (3,470 → 3,471, the new module). `tryStatements` (3,639), `droppedNotAwaited` (239) and every other statistic are the same: BODY's 4 `try` blocks move whole.
- These checkers were run by hand at base and at head, because `dispatch-gates` does not derive the ADR one. All six exit 0 at both. Five print byte-identical output at both (`cmp` clean):
  - `check-adr-symbol-anchors`: 2,384 anchors across 142 records, 466 symbol (440 declaration, 26 literal);
  - `check-scripts-symbol-anchors`: 4,070 anchors;
  - `check-spec-docblock-symbol-anchors`: 5,076 anchors;
  - `check-system-context-census`: 149 elevation read sites;
  - `check-platform-checklist`: 16 areas, 329 items.

  The sixth, `check-adr-anchors`, differs only in the file count and the decision letters, as in the table above.

**5. Gates.**
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives 54 commands for the 2 paths. All 54 ran at head after the full build, and all 54 exited 0.
- `--ran` over the record with each exit code: 54 derived, 54 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, a derived zero. `--tier`: no path-derived mandate.
- `check-governed-merges.mjs --branch HEAD`: NOT governed, 467 changed lines.
- **Docs drift** (`node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ff43b67ea`, exit 0): 0 pages name something this change touched (19 anchors across `plugin-auth`), and 0 release-owned pages. So no doc edit is owed.
- **Serial constraints** (in the claim): 11 PRs are open, and none touches `auth-manager.ts`, the new module's path, or a reader named above. The Version Packages PR #24876 touches `plugin-auth`'s `package.json`, its `CHANGELOG.md` and changesets only. #25530 adds one `scripts/adr-anchors/` entry for a `plugin-security` file, which moves `check-adr-anchors`' totals for whichever lands second, but not this cut's four letters. `origin/main` has moved 2 commits past this base, to `74496c64b0` (#25526 `plugin-approvals`, #25527 `service-settings`). Neither touches `plugin-auth` or `scripts/`.

## Changeset

None: `skip-changeset`, per ruling `6348891160` item 4. The published declarations and export lists are unchanged, and the bundle's bytes move only because code moved inside it.
